synopsis: The corpus distinguishes training data for teaching the detector, validation data for choosing settings, and test data for honest scoring; judging data must have played no part in building or tuning the system [f12882, f14471]. For this program, validation and estimation data must be real or physically independent of the training-data generator, with different assets, sites, people and generator documented in a data-lineage record [f7100, f14472]. Studies from 2023–2026 generally support mixing synthetic and real training data in data-poor construction settings, but synthetic data has not been shown to replace real validation, and no peer-reviewed study was found establishing synthetic-only field-level collision-avoidance reliability across the stated heavy-machine conditions [f7412, f6684, f7103]. Practical safeguards include holding out entire sites or scenario families, maintaining separate tuning, validation and audit sets, preallocating physical datasets before prototype testing, and never tuning against final validation data [f6675, f6676, f8226, f11032]. Learned models and automatic labelers inherit training-domain limitations and biases; improving virtual metrics while held-out real performance stalls signals simulator overfitting [f4487, f12785, f12892]. Warning-fleet logs could supply independent replay evidence, but their validation use depends on ground truth, consent and data rights, and customer-site recording permissions were not examined [f7932, f8246, f8247].
